status: Exploratory follow-up designed after the published NEU-DET results were inspected.
validation: Use the original 360 validation images. Fit thresholds and select paths before evaluating their new test readouts. Retain whole score ties, same-class matching at IoU 0.50, and the allowance of 36 false boxes.
path_selection: At 480, compare both OpenVINO heads of A-E and the deployed dense path of each historical model. Use the existing independently calibrated global thresholds and their live pipeline timings. Relative to A one-to-one, require no more than 1 pp loss in mAP and 2 pp in every class recall for seed 0 and the paired three-seed mean. Require each fitted path to meet the false-box allowance. Rank eligible paths by mean seed-level validation p95 for speed, or by mean validation macro recall for a recall-first comparison. Secondary ties use the other measure, then path name. Publish session overlap and keep the speed choice as primary.
class_thresholds: At 480 for each of the 36 OpenVINO checkpoint/head paths, compare a single threshold with six class thresholds. Maximize mean class recall under the total budget; separately maximize the lowest of the six class recalls, then mean recall. Ties prefer fewer false boxes and then higher thresholds in dataset class order. Report validation and frozen test object and image counts. These are quality analyses; no latency value is transferred to a class-specific policy.
size_thresholds: Independently fit a global threshold for each of the 60 existing one-to-one static OpenVINO graphs (A-E, three seeds, four sizes). Report recall, AP and realized false boxes on the original split. The original common-cutoff size timings remain labeled with their own operating policy.
sensitivity: Repeat the original one-to-one architecture eligibility calculation and the unified 480-pixel head comparison at per-class recall losses of 1, 2, 3 and 5 pp. Retain the original AP and false-box limits, baselines and timing/tie rules for each experiment.
image_outcomes: For an annotated frame count any accepted box as a rejection alarm. Independently count frames with a correctly localized, correctly classified defect, frames flagged only by unmatched boxes, and frames with no flag. Clean-frame false-rejection rate requires independently labeled clean material.
